hooks.command: case "$CLAUDE_FILE_PATH" in *frontend/*.ts|*frontend/*.tsx) [ -x frontend/node_modules/.bin/eslint ] && frontend/node_modules/.bin/eslint --fix "$CLAUDE_FILE_PATH"; true ;; *backend/*.cs) command -v dotnet >/dev/null 2>&1 && dotnet format backend/Chh.sln --include "$CLAUDE_FILE_PATH" --no-restore; true ;; esac

echo '[hook] BLOCKED: Jira status transitions are prohibited for this pipeline — root CLAUDE.md / .claude/agents/orchestrator.md Orchestrator Rule 10. The only permitted Jira write is a comment via gap-flag-skill (Owner:BA gaps); status transitions have no exception. If this is a legitimate manual transition, do it directly in the Jira UI instead of through the agent.' 1>&2; exit 2

_comment: PostToolUse lints the just-edited file by path: frontend/*.ts(x) via the frontend-local ESLint --fix (targeted rule fixes only), backend/*.cs via 'dotnet format --include' against backend/Chh.sln (assumes a prior restore; add 'dotnet restore' first if this ever runs on a clean checkout). Prettier was deliberately left OUT of the frontend branch — verified live that 'prettier --write' against this codebase's existing (wider-than-80-col) JSX style reflows ~75 lines from a single-line edit with no .prettierrc pinning the actual convention; add it back only after a .prettierrc matching the real style is committed. Both branches end in a bare 'true' so a lint/format failure is surfaced as output but never fails the hook itself. PreToolUse hard-blocks (exit 2) any Jira transition call, enforcing Orchestrator Rule 10 at the tool level instead of relying only on agents following the rule — matcher covers both the mcp__atlassian__* and legacy mcp__claude_ai_Atlassian__* tool names seen across this project's MCP server changes, plus a jira_transition_issue fallback. Test commands (dotnet test / npm run test) intentionally aren't wired into this PreToolUse hook, since Rule 10 disallows the transition outright regardless of test status.
